purpose: Vetted transcription of NAPIC official commercial property indicators SPECIFIC TO KUALA LUMPUR sub-district / precinct level, and KL-only historical overhang and supply-pipeline series, for use on myproperty.investmquest.com. Companion file to data/napic-commercial.json (state-level national comparison, produced by a separate concurrent session) — this file goes one level deeper, into KL's own internal precinct breakdown. Produced 2026-08-12 by transcribing already-downloaded NAPIC quarterly Excel tables; no new downloads were made. Promoted to v1 on 2026-08-12 after human spot-check of sub-district cells and new history values against the source XLS.
discipline: Every value is transcribed directly from a cell in one of the official NAPIC quarterly Excel tables listed in rawFilesUsed below (already downloaded to disk for a companion transcription task). Nothing is interpolated, estimated, smoothed, or sourced from any second-hand republication. Missing/not-disclosed by NAPIC ('ND'/'NA' in source cells, meaning the precinct has no stock in that category) = null. Every value carries a source.file/sheet/row citation. No derived values appear in this file except where explicitly flagged with a 'basis' field.

notes.tableStructureTable8: Table 8 lays each state out as: a state-name header row, then one 3-row block per price band (row1=Unit Launched, row2=Unsold Units, row3=Value RM Million), ending in a 'TOTAL' 3-row block (same row1/row2/row3 pattern, with 'TOTAL' printed in the Price Range column of row1). The value this file reports as *_unsold_units / *_unsold_value_rm_million is always the TOTAL block's row2/row3 — i.e. the state's aggregate unsold-completed ('overhang') count and RM value across all price bands, matching the same convention used in the companion data/napic-commercial.json file. Column layout (0-indexed): col11 = SHOP Total, col13 = SOHO, col14 = Serviced Apartment.
notes.shoppingComplexVsCentre: Table 2.1 ('Kompleks Perniagaan'/Shopping Complex, 3,386.19 '000 sm existing, 115 buildings) and Table 3.1 ('Pusat Beli-Belah'/Shopping Centre, 2,998.84 '000 sm existing, 83 buildings) are two distinct NAPIC series for W.P. Kuala Lumpur, not one a subset relabelling of the other — see data/napic-commercial.json notes.shoppingComplexVsCentre for the same distinction at national level. Both are reported here in full since they share the same 24 precinct names, letting the two be compared precinct-by-precinct if useful; Shopping Centre is consistently the narrower of the two (fewer/smaller buildings in several precincts, e.g. Bukit Bintang/Jalan Raja Chulan 570.52 vs 502.81 '000sm, Pudu Area 192.47 vs 139.72 '000sm), consistent with it being a stricter/narrower classification.
notes.buildingCountCrossCheck: For every one of the 3 sub-district tables (PBO, Shopping Complex, Shopping Centre), the sum of total_buildings across all listed precincts was verified to equal the state TOTAL row's total_buildings exactly (PBO: 306+113=419; Shopping Complex: sum of 24 precincts=115; Shopping Centre: sum of 24 precincts=83), and the sum of total_existing_space_000sm across precincts matches the state total to within rounding (<=0.01 '000sm on 3,000-9,600 '000sm bases). This confirms the precinct lists are complete (no precinct rows were skipped).
notes.ndPrecincts: 5 precincts (Stadium Area, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Jalan Klang Lama, Jalan Pahang, Jalan Sentul) show zero existing space in both Shopping Complex and Shopping Centre tables for Q1 2026, with occupancy_rate_pct/availability_rate_pct recorded by NAPIC as 'ND'/'NA' respectively (transcribed here as null) — i.e. these precincts currently have no shopping complex/centre stock recorded, not a data-quality gap.
notes.pboPrecinctGranularity: Unlike the retail tables' 24-precinct breakdown, the PBO (Purpose-Built Office) sub-district table for W.P. Kuala Lumpur (Table 1.1) only splits into 2 precincts: 'City Centre (Seksyen 1-100, Bandar KL)' and 'Outside City Centre (Luar Seksyen 1-100, Bandar KL)'. This is the full granularity NAPIC publishes for KL office space — not a truncation on this file's part.
notes.stockPipelineSubAreas: The Jadual Stok Harta Perdagangan TABLE 2 sub-area names (Bandar Kuala Lumpur, Bandar Petaling Jaya, Mukim Ampang, Mukim Batu, Mukim Cheras, Mukim Hulu Kelang, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, Mukim Petaling, Mukim Setapak) are NAPIC's own mukim/administrative-area classification for tracking supply pipeline, and are NOT the same set of names as the CBSA occupancy tables' 24 commercial precincts (e.g. 'Bangsar', 'Bukit Bintang'). The two classification schemes should not be merged or cross-mapped without further verification; they are kept as separate datasets in this file (subdistricts vs pipeline.subdistricts).
notes.anchorVerification_2026_08_12: All anchors given in the task brief were checked and matched exactly, to the unit: SOHO overhang 2021=457, 2022=788, 2024=645, Q4 2025=1124, Q1 2026=793; Shop overhang 2021=66, 2022=82, 2024=11, Q4 2025=10, Q1 2026=10; SA overhang 2021=4695, Q3 2025=4687, Q4 2025=3964, Q1 2026=4181; supply-pipeline existing stock shop=30973/SOHO=12266/SA=153646. notes.historicalOfficeOccupancy_2026_08_12: Built to test whether the Q1 2026 City Centre vs Outside City Centre occupancy gap (6.8pp) is a new/widening pattern or business-as-usual, time-boxed to a single research pass. Method: located the working NAPIC CBSA download URL pattern from an already-cached page in this session's scratchpad, generalised it to https://napic.jpph.gov.my/storage/app/media//3-penerbitan/Shahrul/Bahagian%20Inventori%20Harta%20Tanah/Laporan%20Jadual%20CBSA/{Quarter%20Year}/Jadual%20Penghunian%20dan%20Ketersediaan%20Ruang%20Bangunan%20Perdagangan%20{Quarter%20Year}.xls, and successfully downloaded Q1 2025, Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 (HTTP 200 on first attempt for all three; Q1 2026 was already on disk from the companion transcription task). Q2 2025 was not located/attempted within the time-box and is not part of this series — the 4 points below are Q1'25/Q3'25/Q4'25/Q1'26 only, not a complete quarterly run. Parsed with xlrd; TABLE 1.1 rows 7/9/11 (0-indexed 6/8/10) confirmed as W.P KUALA LUMPUR total/City Centre/Outside City Centre for every file by title-row text match, same convention as pbo_purpose_built_office above. Q1 2026 values reproduced from this history (73.38356446611137% / 66.62985851403141%) were cross-checked against pbo_purpose_built_office.precincts above and match to full float precision — confirms both extractions read the same source cells.

office_net_absorption_derived_2026_08_13.purpose: Net absorption (change in occupied space) and stock change (change in total existing space), KL total / City Centre / Outside City Centre, derived from the 4-quarter series already in historical_cbsa_office_occupancy_kl above. Built to answer directly: is the Q4'25->Q1'26 occupancy-rate rise (70.94% -> 71.87%) driven by genuine demand growth or by a shrinking stock base.

series.note: Q2 2025 not sampled by the underlying historical_cbsa_office_occupancy_kl dataset — this interval is a two-quarter combined change, not a single-quarter reading.

office_net_absorption_derived_2026_08_13.keyFinding_stockContraction: KL total existing space fell from 9,662.34 to 9,633.72 ('000 sm) between Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 - a -28.62 ('000 sm) contraction (derived, see series above), even as occupied space rose +69.01 ('000 sm) in the same quarter. The occupancy-rate rise from 70.94% to 71.87% is therefore driven by both genuine positive net absorption AND a shrinking denominator, not demand alone. This dataset does not carry a NAPIC-published completions figure for the PBO/office series (unlike the shop/SOHO/SA supply-pipeline table, which does), so the stock contraction's cause (completions falling short of buildings withdrawn/reclassified out of NAPIC's CBSA register, e.g. redevelopment, demolition, or scope revision) is inferred from the stock figures themselves, not confirmed against a separate completions line - flagged as inference, not a NAPIC-stated cause.
office_net_absorption_derived_2026_08_13.keyFinding_ccConcentration: In the same Q4'25->Q1'26 quarter, City Centre absorbed +67.69 ('000 sm) of the citywide +69.01 ('000 sm) net absorption - 98.1% of the citywide total (derived: 67.69/69.01) - while Outside City Centre absorbed just +1.32 ('000 sm). The most recent quarter's demand growth is almost entirely a City Centre phenomenon, consistent with this report's flight-to-quality reading of the CC/OCC occupancy gap elsewhere in Section II.
office_net_absorption_derived_2026_08_13.keyFinding_priorQuarterReversal: In the prior quarter (Q3'25->Q4'25), City Centre's net absorption was NEGATIVE (-5.40 '000 sm - occupied space fell) even as its stock also fell (-20.61 '000 sm), while Outside City Centre gained stock (+48.33 '000 sm) and had the larger positive net absorption (+15.23 '000 sm) of the two segments that quarter. The Q4'25->Q1'26 concentration of absorption in City Centre (previous finding) is therefore a reversal from the prior quarter, not a steady one-directional trend - two data points, not yet a confirmed pattern.

office_yield_caprate_search_2026_08_13.purpose: Attempt to source a verifiable KL prime office investment yield / cap rate figure from Knight Frank, Savills or CBRE for the Capital Markets chapter, per task brief instruction to cite if found with a checkable source, or explicitly decline if not.
searchesPerformed: WebSearch: Knight Frank Kuala Lumpur office investment yield cap rate 2025 2026
WebSearch: Savills OR CBRE OR Knight Frank Kuala Lumpur prime office cap rate percent 2026

office_yield_caprate_search_2026_08_13.result: No KL/Malaysia office prime yield or cap rate percentage was found with a checkable source and figure within this research pass. Knight Frank's Investment Yield Guide and CBRE's Asia Pacific Cap Rate Survey both appear to exist as publications that likely carry this figure, but neither was accessible in a form that surfaced the actual Malaysia/KL number (PDFs either did not cover the market or were index/presentation shells; landing pages did not expose the underlying table).
office_yield_caprate_search_2026_08_13.decision: This report does not cite a KL office cap rate / investment yield figure anywhere. NAPIC does not publish one, and this session could not verify one from Knight Frank, Savills or CBRE within budget. Declining to cite an unverified figure is treated as the correct professional posture, not a gap to paper over with an estimate.
